candidates.name: Sextic-twist Mobius <-> cubic-theta duality
candidates.lean: Moments/, GaussSum/, Eisenstein/, Reflection/, Descent/, Inversion/, QuadraticSieve/ (Hecke/InverseAmplificationRaw.lean: HeckeInverseAmplification.RawMoment); together ~56% of the 18,626-declaration zeta DAG
candidates.statement: Twist the Mobius sum of a Hecke character over Q(sqrt-3) by the sextic residue symbol chi_n(u) and average over u in a box longer than the column range. Poisson summation in u produces sextic Gauss sums gamma_{-1}(n), which combine with mu(n) through gamma_2(n)^3=mu(n)alpha(n) into cubic Gauss sums, i.e. Kubota-Patterson theta coefficients. The theta transformation turns the dual sums into quadratically twisted sums controlled by the quadratic large sieve, and a Heath-Brown-type recursion closes the estimate. The family therefore has square-root cancellation on average (A04 = Q eq:raw-moment). Q uses the same duality inside a probe whose principal Poisson row is 1/L_F (Q16, Q18).

candidates.name: Family bootstrap on beta_* with saturated two-witness zero detector
candidates.lean: Hecke/ZeroSupremum.lean; Supremum.lean; Detector/ (11.9% of zeta DAG)
candidates.statement: Suppose the supremum beta_* of zero real parts over the whole primitive Hecke family exceeds sigma_0. Measure every Poisson row against Z^{C(beta_*)}. Rows with zeros above the floor yield simultaneous large inverse and plain Dirichlet polynomials (saturated witnesses), which moment bounds count. This replaces DR's GRH.

candidates.name: Weighted Frobenius interpolation determinant for Landau-Siegel zeros
candidates.statement: In K=Q(sqrt d, sqrt2), form the determinant of monomial rows theta^{a1}(sigma theta)^{a2}(sigma tau theta)^{a3} over a box of points, rows chosen greedily in the weight order a1+H(a2+a3). For inert p>H, theta^p == sigma(theta) or sigma tau(theta) mod p, so a unitriangular row replacement shows p^{sum floor(a1/p)} | Delta. A Siegel zero makes inert primes carry mass ~log U, while the archimedean bound only allows (3/4)log U.

prompt_arms.O (open): Prove a fixed zero-free half-plane for Hecke L-functions over Q(sqrt-3) (or for zeta). Context L.
prompt_arms.R (route): Also give Littlewood's equivalence and HB00 eq (2) (the identity gamma_2(n)^3=mu(n)alpha(n)), and ask for a family of sums whose dual is automorphic.

P-C1.equivalence: A hit must (i) embed the Mobius sum (or 1/L) of the target into a family twisted by higher-order residue symbols over Z[omega] whose Poisson/finite-Fourier dual has cubic Gauss/theta coefficients (sextic or an equivalent order-6 construction), and (ii) say how the target is recovered (rows u=p^6, or a principal Poisson row). Using cubic or quadratic twists without automorphic duality is a miss.
P-C1.metrics: discovery curve hit-rate(k); also record proposals that reach (i) but not (ii).

P-C2.equivalence: a family-supremum bootstrap with a zero detector producing large Dirichlet polynomials

P-C3.context: Give Q Part I (11/12) in full
P-C3.equivalence: a prime-slot compensation that cancels the scalar prime Euler contribution and improves the exponent below 11/12.

prompt_arms.O: Prove (1-beta)log q >= c for real zeros of real primitive characters. Context L (FI 2018 Sec 5 included).
prompt_arms.R: Also give Cantor-Straus/Dobrowolski in context (positive-control arm for the Lehmer analogy).

P-C6.equivalence: A hit must build a nonzero algebraic integer (determinant or resultant) from conjugates of elements of a field containing sqrt d, use theta^p == sigma(theta) mod p for chi(p)=-1 to get p-adic divisibility over many primes, and compare with an archimedean bound using the Siegel-zero inert-prime bias. Weighted ordering not required for a partial hit; required for a full hit.
P-C6.metrics: hit rate per arm; the gap between O and R measures how much of the step is the Lehmer-to-Siegel bridge.

open_questions: Compile result from the orchestrator (all four comparators, axioms only propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice). This is the decisive trust input; if it passes, D3 vs D2 is the only question left for this family.

Read DR in full (arXiv 2109.07463 per a search summary): does any step embed Mobius or 1/L sums into a higher-order-twist family whose dual is theta coefficients? If yes, C1 -> N2 and the automorphic bridge becomes a known route.

Is A04 (square-root cancellation over rows H=D^{1+theta}, i.e. a dual mean square E(H,X)<<X for cubic-Gauss coefficients) consistent with DR's GRH-conditional sharpness of Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve? An expert check of DR's extremal configuration against A12/A14 is needed.
Does the Lean 7/8 proof really bypass Part I (no beta_*<=11/12 input)? If yes, the Lean argument is a different, possibly simpler route than Q, worth extracting.
Expert opinion (transcendence/Lehmer community, e.g. Voutier, Dubickas, Fischler): is the weighted Frobenius determinant (C6) materially beyond Cantor-Straus? This decides N2 vs N3 for C6.

Downstream speedup: family 029 re-uses the C1 device over all cyclotomic fields containing mu_12 to get a Hecke half-plane 1-10^{-6}. This is a genuine reuse-of-device datum (not a corollary), but it is model-produced and same-release; treat it separately in the downstream test. Families 142 and 182 are corollary-only.

The Hecke comparator's L-function is defined in the challenge file; a reviewer should confirm IdealBridge.lean's LFunction_eq_ideal_tsum and holomorphy lemmas (outside the comparator) and that Character covers all finite-order Hecke characters (class number 1 argument).
